title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 184 (Disclosure of interest by director)

content.overview: Section 184 requires every director to disclose his concern or interest in any company or companies or bodies corporate, firms, or other association of individuals, including shareholding, at the first meeting of the Board in which he participates as a director and thereafter at the first meeting of the Board in every financial year or whenever there is any change. A director who is interested in a contract or arrangement with a body corporate, firm or other entity shall disclose the nature of his concern or interest at the meeting of the Board in which the contract or arrangement is discussed, and shall not participate in such meeting. A contract or arrangement entered into without disclosure is voidable at the option of the company.
content.glance: Director discloses concern/interest (including shareholding) at first Board meeting as director, at first Board meeting each year, and on change; interested director discloses nature of interest and does not participate; non-disclosure makes contract voidable at company’s option.
content.study: Every director shall at the first meeting of the Board in which he participates as a director and thereafter at the first meeting of the Board in every financial year or whenever there is any change in the disclosures already made, disclose his concern or interest in any company or companies or bodies corporate, firms, or other association of individuals which shall include the shareholding, in such manner as may be prescribed. Every director who is in any way, whether directly or indirectly, concerned or interested in a contract or arrangement or proposed contract or arrangement entered into or to be entered into with a body corporate in which such director or such director in association with any other director holds more than two per cent shareholding, or with a firm or other entity in which such director is a partner, owner or member, shall disclose the nature of his concern or interest at the meeting of the Board in which the contract or arrangement is discussed and shall not participate in such meeting. A contract or arrangement entered into by the company without disclosure or with participation by the interested director is voidable at the option of the company. Current-law framing: confirm general disclosure (first meeting / annual / change); test specific disclosure and non-participation on the contract item; apply voidability on breach. Distinct from related-party transaction approval under section 188.

sections.heading: General Disclosure
sections.body: Concern or interest in companies, bodies corporate, firms or associations (including shareholding) disclosed at the first Board meeting as director, at the first Board meeting each financial year, and on any change.

sections.heading: Contract-Specific Disclosure
sections.body: Director interested in a contract or arrangement discloses the nature of concern or interest at the Board meeting discussing it.

sections.heading: Non-Participation
sections.body: Interested director shall not participate in the Board meeting on that contract or arrangement.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: Contract or arrangement entered without disclosure, or with participation by the interested director, is voidable at the option of the company.

examples.title: Annual disclosure
examples.body: A director updates the Board at the first meeting of the financial year with current shareholdings in other companies. Section 184’s general disclosure duty is met for that year until a change occurs.

examples.title: Participation after non-disclosure
examples.body: A director interested in a proposed contract neither discloses nor abstains, and the Board approves the contract. The contract is voidable at the option of the company under s. 184.

hypotheticals.question: Does disclosure under s. 184 replace the need for s. 188 related-party approval?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 184 is a disclosure and non-participation rule. Section 188 is a separate approval regime for specified related-party transactions. Both may apply on the same facts.

distinctions.title: Disclosure of interest (s. 184) vs related-party transactions (s. 188)
distinctions.right: Board/member approval route for specified RPTs

misconceptions.trap: Once a director has disclosed interests at appointment, no further disclosure is needed.
misconceptions.correction: Disclosure is required at the first Board meeting each financial year and whenever there is any change in the disclosures already made.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 184 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm general disclosure timeline. II. Test contract-specific disclosure and non-participation. III. Apply voidability. IV. Distinguish s. 188. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Disclosure facts; participation; contract status; precise relief.

examTips: General disclosure: first meeting, annual, on change.
Contract item: disclose and do not participate.
